title: Phase 2.1: Resolve visible UX and formatting issues
body:
## Goal

Make dates and dataset expiry easy to understand, explain when Upload is unavailable, and give every major interaction state distinct feedback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All application-generated dates, including chart labels, expiry text, and any status text, use consistent English date formatting in browsers configured for Turkish or English. Calendar dates still represent the same dates in either browser.
- [ ] The dashboard's Expires fact shows relative time as its primary text (for example, “Expires in 23 hours”); an exact local expiry timestamp may appear as secondary text or a tooltip. Expired datasets continue to show the existing expired-state screen.
- [ ] While Upload is disabled because a CSV or currency is missing, the upload screen displays “Select a CSV file and currency to continue.” in association with the button. Once both valid selections are present, Upload becomes enabled and the helper no longer misstates the reason.
- [ ] Loading, empty, disabled, successful upload, warning, and error states each have visible, understandable feedback on the upload and dashboard screens; warning and error states remain distinguishable without color alone.
- [ ] The native file picker keeps the browser's own localization.

## Out of scope

- None of this plan item's work is deferred. The native file picker is browser controlled; its text is not an application string. Phase 2 product guardrails in `_docs/plan.md` still apply.

## Constraints

- Work in `frontend/src/pages/`, `frontend/src/components/`, and `frontend/src/lib/` as needed; follow `_docs/design-system.md` for all UI changes.
- Preserve existing fixed labels, “gross sales” terminology, keyboard access, and status/error semantics. Add a rule to the design-system document for any new visual treatment.
- Coordinate with item 2 for chart bucket labels, and item 5 for component coverage. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.2: Mark partial trend buckets and explain bucketing
body:
## Goal

Make the date coverage of every daily, weekly, and monthly trend bucket clear, especially when the selected range cuts through a week or month.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For the active inclusive date range, bucket coverage is evaluated against each calendar bucket: day, Monday–Sunday week, or calendar month. A bucket truncated by the dataset or selected range is marked “Partial period” in its tooltip; a full bucket is not.
- [ ] A one-day daily bucket is evaluated by the same rule and is complete for the app's date-only data contract; a one-day slice of a weekly or monthly bucket is partial.
- [ ] A partial first or last weekly or monthly bucket has a visible covered date-range label (for example, “Dec 29–31”) wherever only “Week of Dec 29” or a month name would hide the truncation. The tooltip includes the year and “Partial period”.
- [ ] A range entirely inside one week or month displays that sole bucket as partial when appropriate; a range spanning a year boundary, leap day, or exact bucket boundary labels its coverage correctly.
- [ ] Trend gross-sales totals and the existing automatic granularity thresholds (up to 90 days daily, over 90 days through two years weekly, then monthly) are unchanged.
- [ ] Automated checks cover first, last, exact-boundary, single-bucket, and year-crossing cases. README or API documentation explains Monday-start weeks, inclusive range boundaries, and partial-bucket presentation.

## Out of scope

- No work from this item is deferred. A manual granularity picker and period-over-period comparison are outside Phase 2.

## Constraints

- Existing API trend data exposes `bucket_start`; determine coverage from the analytics range and calendar bucket bounds without treating zero-sales days as missing days. Change the API contract only if necessary, and update `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` and API tests if it changes.
- Likely areas: `backend/app/analytics/trend.py`, `frontend/src/components/TrendChart.tsx`, related tests, and `README.md`. Follow `_docs/plan.md`, `_docs/design-system.md`, and `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.3: Complete backend validation and metrics unit coverage
body:
## Goal

Make every CSV business rule and core metric calculation independently verifiable with deterministic pytest cases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Focused tests cover all six required fields: `order_id`, `order_date`, `product_id`, `product_name`, `quantity`, and `unit_price`; missing/blank values, bad types, invalid and future dates, quantity and price boundaries, duplicate `(order_id, product_id)`, and conflicting names for one product ID are checked.
- [ ] Tests verify that zero price and ignored extra columns produce the documented warning codes and an accepted import, while any invalid row rejects the whole file.
- [ ] Every documented CSV validation error code and warning code in the README has a direct assertion of its code and relevant row or field. Cases at and just beyond the 50 MB and 500,000-row defaults are checked with focused limits or boundary fixtures, avoiding giant fixtures.
- [ ] Daily, Monday-start weekly, and monthly aggregation are checked at granularity thresholds and date boundaries, including gaps and partial first/last buckets.
- [ ] Gross sales, distinct order count, units sold, average order value (including zero-order range), and top-product ranking/tie behavior are checked against hand-calculated expected values.
- [ ] Each business-rule failure points to a named test and assertion rather than only a broad snapshot. `uv run pytest` passes.

## Out of scope

- No required validation rule or metric is deferred. API journey coverage belongs to item 4; browser behavior belongs to item 6.

## Constraints

- Extend existing `backend/tests/test_validation_*.py`, `test_kpis.py`, `test_trend.py`, and `test_top_products.py` where possible. Current coverage is already extensive; fill specific gaps rather than duplicating passing cases.
- Treat `README.md` Dataset contract/Error codes and `_docs/plan.md` Metrics and Dashboard as the current contract. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before tests; use isolated small datasets and controlled dates. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.4: Verify upload-to-dashboard API and dataset lifecycle
body:
## Goal

Prove the complete dataset lifecycle through the API, including authentication, expiry, cleanup, and consistent filtered analytics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A valid multipart CSV plus currency returns 201 with dataset ID, bearer token, warnings and initial summary; the resulting DuckDB is readable through authorized metadata/analytics endpoints without a browser.
- [ ] After a successful import, no raw CSV remains in the temporary or dataset directory; an invalid upload leaves no usable dataset, DuckDB artifact, or raw CSV.
- [ ] Requests with a wrong dataset ID, absent bearer token, malformed token, or token issued for another dataset cannot read metadata or analytics. The matching token works before expiry.
- [ ] At exactly the configured expiry instant the dataset is inaccessible, and startup/periodic cleanup removes expired files according to the default 24-hour TTL and configured interval; earlier datasets remain usable.
- [ ] Applying the same inclusive start/end dates to KPI, trend and top-product results yields internally consistent values and rankings, including a no-sales range and invalid-range response.
- [ ] These checks run through `TestClient` or an isolated process, use temporary dataset storage and a controlled clock, and pass under `uv run pytest`.

## Out of scope

- No required lifecycle behavior is deferred. Frontend interaction checks belong to item 5; browser checks belong to item 6.

## Constraints

- Extend `backend/tests/test_upload_endpoint.py`, `test_auth.py`, `test_cleanup.py`, and `test_analytics_endpoint.py` where needed; preserve the existing FastAPI/DuckDB API and privacy contract in `README.md` and `_docs/plan.md`.
- Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`; never touch the real `DATASET_DIR`, wait for real expiry, or log raw values/tokens. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.5: Complete frontend component and accessibility coverage
body:
## Goal

Use Vitest and React Testing Library to verify the visible upload and dashboard behavior, including errors, empty data and accessibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests show file and currency selection controlling Upload's disabled/enabled state and its helper or validation feedback, including clearing/replacing a file.
- [ ] Tests show actionable validation errors and accepted warnings, including their visible labels, roles, dismiss behavior, and safe rendering of server text.
- [ ] The four KPI cards show correct formatted values, counts, and selected currency, including zeros and large values.
- [ ] Date-range selection updates visible KPI/trend/top-product results; Reset restores the full-range view; an invalid range gives visible feedback without applying it.
- [ ] Loading, no-sales, API failure with Retry, missing session/unauthorized, and expired-dataset states each have the expected visible response.
- [ ] Deterministic fixtures cover daily/weekly/monthly trend and top-product chart/table content, including the partial-bucket display from item 2.
- [ ] Tests confirm visible labels for file, currency, date fields and buttons; named chart regions/text alternatives and alert/status semantics remain present. Keyboard-only navigation can reach and operate key controls.
- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run typecheck` pass from `frontend/`.

## Out of scope

- No required component behavior is deferred. Full browser flow coverage belongs to item 6.

## Constraints

- Extend co-located `frontend/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` files; use existing Vitest, React Testing Library, jsdom setup and deterministic fetch stubs. Test visible behavior, not component internals.
- Follow `_docs/design-system.md` and `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`; item 1 and item 2 should be merged before finalizing their related expectations. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.6: Expand Playwright coverage of the primary journeys
body:
## Goal

Provide a small deterministic browser suite that demonstrates the core upload, validation, filtering, restart, and expiry journeys locally and in CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visitor can click “Try sample data” and see populated KPI, trend, and top-product views from a deterministic sample.
- [ ] Uploading a known valid CSV with a selected currency opens the dashboard and shows expected KPI values and charts.
- [ ] Uploading a known invalid CSV stays on the upload screen and shows actionable rejection details with the expected code/row/field where applicable.
- [ ] Applying a date range changes visible dashboard values and granularity; Reset restores the original values.
- [ ] “Analyze another file” returns to the upload screen and the prior dataset is no longer available.
- [ ] An expired dataset shows the expired experience, using controlled server/test configuration rather than a real 24-hour wait.
- [ ] `npm run e2e` runs without manual steps against the local app and `E2E_BASE_URL` container path; the same browser suite passes in CI. Selectors use roles/labels or stable test hooks, and data/clock behavior is deterministic.

## Out of scope

- No planned browser journey is deferred. Cross-browser matrix and visual snapshots are outside this item.

## Constraints

- Extend `frontend/e2e/` and its Playwright config. The repo currently has one sample happy-path spec; keep the suite small and follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` for isolation and cleanup.
- Respect `_docs/design-system.md` when a browser finding requires a UI fix. Items 1–5 define the behavior this suite verifies. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.7: Finalize the one-container distribution
body:
## Goal

Make the full React and FastAPI app reproducible in one documented Docker image with safe runtime defaults and lifecycle behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean checkout can build the image and launch the complete app with the single Docker command documented in `README.md`; the SPA and `/api` respond from the same origin and deep links load.
- [ ] `Dockerfile` uses build and runtime stages; the final runtime image does not include the Node build toolchain unless a documented runtime need is found.
- [ ] The application runs as a non-root user, and created DuckDB files stay within the configured application dataset directory with the documented private permissions.
- [ ] `/api/health` returns the expected healthy response and Docker health status becomes healthy after startup; it reports failure if the server stops responding.
- [ ] Explicit defaults for upload size, request/startup timeout where applicable, dataset TTL, cleanup interval, and storage path are documented and match runtime behavior. The 50 MB and 500,000-row upload limits remain enforced.
- [ ] `.dockerignore` excludes development output, local data, credentials, and secrets from the build context.
- [ ] Container startup schedules or performs expiry cleanup, and shutdown stops background cleanup cleanly; this behavior is verified with the packaged image or equivalent integration evidence.

## Out of scope

- No packaging requirement is deferred. A multi-instance deployment or durable upload history is outside Phase 2.

## Constraints

- Existing `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `compose.yaml`, `backend/app/main.py`, and `backend/app/config.py` already implement much of this; verify then close gaps. Keep one-instance DuckDB semantics.
- Follow `README.md` configuration/privacy contract and `_docs/plan.md` architecture; tests require `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Read `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` before changing tests. Add no dependency in `pyproject.toml` without asking, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: Phase 2.8: Complete CI and security quality gates
body:
## Goal

Make every pull request prove the application can lint, type-check, test, build, and pass a browser smoke flow from a clean checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pull requests and default-branch pushes run Ruff lint and format checks, mypy for backend app code, and backend pytest unit/integration tests; each failing command fails its job.
- [ ] CI runs frontend type checking, linting, Vitest, and a production bundle build. A broken bundle build fails CI even if type checking passes.
- [ ] CI builds the Docker image, starts it, checks `/api/health` and SPA delivery, and runs the Playwright smoke suite against that built application.
- [ ] Dependency/security scanning covers both Python and npm manifests/lockfiles or equivalent repository dependency alerts; a documented finding policy states which severity fails CI, and a deliberately failing scan cannot leave CI green.
- [ ] Dependency caches cover package downloads/tool data only; generated datasets, uploaded files, secrets, and runtime DuckDB files are never cached or uploaded as artifacts.
- [ ] The README lists the same essential local commands as CI. A clean checkout can execute them without hidden local configuration.

## Out of scope

- No CI gate from the Phase 2 plan is deferred. Release automation and deployment credentials are outside this item.

## Constraints

- Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `README.md`, and tool config as needed. Current workflow already has backend/frontend checks and a container browser run; add explicit production build and security scan coverage, and align it with item 6.
- Use minimal read-only token permissions and no secrets for untrusted pull requests. Follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md` and `AGENTS.md`; request approval before adding a dependency to `pyproject.toml`.

title: Phase 2.9: Publish a sample-only public demo
body:
## Goal

Publish a public dashboard that uses the deterministic sample only and cannot accept arbitrary customer CSV uploads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A public demo URL loads successfully and a visitor can explore the full dashboard using “Try sample data” without supplying a file.
- [ ] The hosted UI visibly says it accepts sample data only, hides or disables arbitrary CSV selection/upload, and links directly to the self-hosting instructions in `README.md`.
- [ ] The hosted API is configured in public demo mode; a direct `POST /api/datasets` with an arbitrary multipart CSV returns the documented 403 `upload_disabled` before its body is imported. Sample creation and sample CSV download still work.
- [ ] The documented self-hosted Docker command continues to allow full CSV upload with default settings.
- [ ] Review of the deployed artifact and configuration finds no embedded secret, private dataset, local filesystem path, or reusable test token. The public URL uses transport appropriate for a public deployment and is linked from the README.
- [ ] Public-demo behavior is verified against the deployed URL after publication, including the direct API rejection and dashboard path.

## Out of scope

- No public-demo safeguard is deferred. Accounts, customer data hosting, and multiple datasets per user are outside Phase 2.

## Constraints

- Reuse existing `PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE=true` behavior in `backend/app/api/datasets.py` and `frontend/src/pages/UploadPage.tsx`; preserve the self-hosted default. Choose a single-instance deployment consistent with local DuckDB storage and capacity limits.
- Follow `README.md` Demo mode/Privacy and `_docs/design-system.md`; item 7 packaging and item 8 CI should be complete first. Do not commit deployment credentials or customer data.

title: Phase 2.10: Finish portfolio and open-source presentation
body:
## Goal

Let a reviewer understand the product, run it, assess its boundaries, and see the same final behavior in docs, media, tests, and public demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `README.md` starts with the user problem, intended scope, a concise architecture explanation/diagram, a working one-command Docker quick start, and a visible public-demo link.
- [ ] README or linked docs fully describe the six-field CSV contract, 50 MB/500,000-row limits, supported currencies, gross-sales/order/units/AOV/top-product definitions, bucket and partial-period rules, date filtering, bearer-token/privacy model, 24-hour expiry/cleanup, demo-versus-self-hosted behavior, and known limitations.
- [ ] Three or four current screenshots show the upload/data-contract screen, KPI and trend dashboard, top-products chart/table, and the validation-error report if it adds useful context; every image matches the released UI and has descriptive alt text.
- [ ] A playable roughly 90-second demo shows sample or valid CSV entry, validation when useful, dashboard exploration and filtering; the recording link or file is accessible from the README.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md`, a clear license file or equivalent license information, and usable GitHub issue templates are present and linked where appropriate.
- [ ] A concise document explains how AI coding tools contributed to specification, implementation, verification, and review, including human review and evidence; statements are accurate for this project.
- [ ] A short roadmap distinguishes completed MVP and Phase 2 work from candidate post-MVP features, without describing candidates as shipped.
- [ ] Links, screenshots, video, architecture diagram, README commands, CI checks, and public demo all reflect the same final product behavior.

## Out of scope

- No required presentation artifact is deferred. Phase 3 features, including period-over-period comparison, remain roadmap candidates.

## Constraints

- Update `README.md`, add documentation/media and repository community files as needed. Use the shipped app and verified commands as the source of truth.
- Follow `_docs/plan.md`, `_docs/design-system.md` for screenshots/UI references, and the Phase 2 guardrails. Complete after items 1–9 so captures and claims represent the final result.
